answer: The falcon I would price into every new account is Confirmed land surveyor licence with land surveyors certification: a licence surveyors renew after boundary audits, and no farm can amortise that across a thousand names. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a licence surveyors renew after boundary audits — so privacy survives, and the fable is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. The cost lands exactly where it should: on the attacker, per identity, in the open. The velvet is public, auditable, and impossible to discount in bulk.
